newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 1.7 pct w/e June 14-Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 1.7 pct w/e June 14-Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 1.7 percent in the first two weeks of fiscal June versus May, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 8.2 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales climbed 7.7 percent in the week ended June 14, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
The week's performance lagged the fast pace of week one, but was still considered respectable by retailers, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
"It was very strong the first week, but the second week toned down," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Sales of summer weather goods, such as fans and air conditioners, were below expections, despite warming temperatures to seasonal levels, he said.

Eilenberg asserted that some retailers were overly optimistic with their store plans for the month of June. He said the stores had forecast an 8.5 percent total-store increase. "We think it will be closer to about 7.4 percent. They were overly optimistic on what they could achieve," he said.
In discount stores, sales in women's apparel is lagging other items, such as childrenswear, menswear and fashion accessories, the Redbook analyst said.
"Womenswear is not that strong in the discount stores," Eilenberg said. "On the other hand, in the department stores and in the chain stores, women's apparel continues to do well."
Looking ahead at total retail sales for the month, Eilenberg said, "(June) is going to be a good month, but not quite as exuberant as the first week."
